rodent

The goal of rodent is to estimate the time-varying reproduction number Rt from case count time series using a deterministic SIR model with piecewise constant transmission rate. Built on the odin2-dust2-monty ecosystem, it supports explicit user-specified change points and full Bayesian inference, enabling interpretable evaluation of intervention effects and epidemic dynamics.

Dependencies

rodent relies on the odin2-dust2-monty ecosystem from RESIDE at Imperial College London. Install these first from r-universe:

install.packages(c("odin2", "dust2", "monty"), 
                 repos = c("https://mrc-ide.r-universe.dev", 
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

Installation

You can install the development version of rodent from GitHub with:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("meaganjharrington/rodent")

Example: 2009 Influenza A(H1N1), Pennsylvania school outbreak

This example uses the Flu2009 dataset from the EpiEstim package. The outbreak comprised 129 cases over 32 days in a school of 369 students, with a known school closure from day 18 to 24.

Change points are set at days 1, 8, 18, and 25, with the third block capturing the period of school closure.

library(odin2)
library(dust2)
library(monty)
library(rodent)
library(EpiEstim)
library(dplyr)


# Prepare incidence data
data(Flu2009)
flu_daily <- Flu2009$incidence |>
  mutate(time = row_number()) |>
  rename(cases = I) |>
  select(time, cases) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Fit rodent
out_flu <- estimate_R_blocks(
  data        = flu_daily,
  N           = 369,
  gamma       = 1 / 2.6,
  beta_breaks = c(1, 8, 18, 25),
  priors = list(mean_beta = log(0.5), sd_beta = 0.5,
                rw_sd_beta = 0.3, mean_I0 = log(5), sd_I0 = 0.5)
)

# View Rt series and plot
# View Rt estimates (median and 95% credible intervals)
head(out_flu$Rt_quantiles)

# View beta estimates
head(out_flu$beta_t_quantiles)

# View susceptible trajectory
head(out_flu$S_quantiles)

# Plot Rt
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(out_flu$Rt_quantiles, aes(x = time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Rt",
       title = "Estimated Rt — Influenza H1N1 2009, Pennsylvania")

Blockwise Rt estimates decline over the outbreak, from ~1.36 in the first block to ~0.86 in the final block, with a notable drop to ~0.41 during the school closure period (days 18–24).

For full methodology and validation results, see the accompanying thesis report.
